title: Conocephalum salebrosum Protocol
author: Zhang, Chi

steps.title: Collect and identify C. salebrosum specimens
steps.instruction: Collect live plants of Conocephalum salebrosum from the field in Illinois and confirm morphological identity as the chemotype with methyl (E)-cinnamate dominance.

steps.title: Establish axenic culture of thallus
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize the collected thallus fragments and place them on sterile culture medium to obtain an axenic (microbe‑free) culture.

steps.title: Grow axenic gametophytes for volatile analysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the axenic culture under appropriate growth conditions until sufficient gametophytic tissue is produced for chemical profiling.

steps.title: Extract volatiles via organic solvent
steps.instruction: Perform an organic extraction on the axenically grown gametophytes to isolate volatile compounds (method details not specified in the source).

steps.title: Analyze extracts by GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Inject the organic extract into a gas chromatography–mass spectrometer (GC‑MS) and record the volatile profile, noting that ten volatiles are detected, with methyl (E)-cinnamate comprising 50.5 % of total volatiles and sabinene representing 20 % of the methyl (E)-cinnamate amount.

steps.title: Perform headspace collection of explants
steps.instruction: Collect headspace volatiles from explants of the axenic C. salebrosum culture using a suitable closed‑system sampling method.

steps.title: Analyze headspace volatiles by GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Run the headspace sample on GC‑MS; identify three dominant compounds, all of which were also present in the organic extract, with methyl (E)-cinnamate again being the most abundant.

steps.title: Retrieve transcriptome data for C. conicum
steps.instruction: Download the vegetative thallus transcriptome of C. conicum from the OneKP portal (https://sites.google.com/a/ualberta.ca/onekp).

steps.title: Identify SABATH unigenes using HMMR search
steps.instruction: Run an HMMR search against the transcriptome using the Methyltransf_7 Pfam profile (Finn et al., 2015) to locate SABATH‑family unigenes.

substeps.instruction: Identify nine unigenes encoding SABATH proteins.
Select the six that are full‑length based on comparison with known SABATH proteins.

steps.title: Select six full‑length CsSABATH genes
steps.instruction: Designate the six full‑length genes as CsSABATH1 through CsSABATH6 (Table S1).

steps.title: Extract RNA and synthesize cDNA from thallus
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from the axenically grown C. salebrosum thallus and reverse‑transcribe it to obtain cDNA for each CsSABATH gene.

steps.title: Amplify full‑length CsSABATH cDNAs by RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Perform RT‑PCR using gene‑specific primers to amplify the complete coding sequences of CsSABATH1‑6.

steps.title: Clone and verify CsSABATH cDNAs
steps.instruction: Insert each amplified cDNA into a suitable cloning vector, transform into competent cells, and confirm sequence integrity (protein lengths range from 383 to 443 amino acids).

steps.title: Conduct semi‑quantitative RT‑PCR (25 cycles) for expression
steps.instruction: Set up semi‑quantitative RT‑PCR reactions for each CsSABATH gene, run 25 PCR cycles, and analyze products on a gel: transcripts for five genes are detected (CsSABATH1 absent), with CsSABATH4 showing the highest expression, CsSABATH2 and CsSABATH6 also high, and CsSABATH3 and CsSABATH5 low.
